study type: Observational comparative study with short-term longitudinal follow-up for the HIE TH group
outcome: Relative abundance of facultative anaerobes and aerobes (e.g., Staphylococcus species)
Relative abundance of strict anaerobes (e.g., Bacteroides genus)
cohort: The study included 28 term newborns with HIE undergoing TH and 19 healthy term newborns as a control group.
finding: Newborns with HIE undergoing TH exhibited altered gut microbiota composition compared to healthy controls, characterized by lower alpha-diversity, increased mean relative abundance of facultative anaerobes/aerobes (e.g., Staphylococcus), and decreased mean relative abundance of strict anaerobes (e.g., Bacteroides and Bifidobacterium).
mod_finding: The study noted that while mode of delivery profoundly influences the gut microbiota, therapeutic hypothermia may exert an independent influence on its composition.
cross-section timing: For the HIE TH group, initial samples were taken at a median age of 68 hours, with a follow-on sample at 151 hours; for the control group, samples were taken at a median age of 34 hours.
